newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip in absence of foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip in absence of foreign buying.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped in quiet trading on Tuesday, as western investors kept away from the market pending news about President Boris Yeltsin's operation, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 21 shares fell by 2.49 points to 171.58 on $17.60 million in volume.

"Even though prices are lower there is no trading going on," said Martin Diggle from Brunswick. "People are reluctant to put any money into the market before the operation on Yeltsin, because they want some confirmation that the operation is going to go well."
Yeltsin said last week he would undergo heart surgery and doctors said he would have a bypass operation.
The market might go up by five to 10 percent on the announcement that the operation was a success, Diggle said.
Andrei Kukk, chief trader from Rinaco-Plus brokerage forecast a seesaw movement on the market with a five percent fall followed by a 2.0 to 2.5 percent rise.
Russian traders lost their nerve in the absence of foreign orders and marked prices down, Diggle said.
"People aren't seeing any buying and when people do not see any foreign buying they tend to become nervous and mark prices lower," he said.
Samit Yakovlev, a trader from United City Bank, said some foreign operators sold shares hoping to buy later at lower prices.
"It's the most quiet day we've had in the past several weeks," Diggle said.

Mosnenergo fell to $0.960/$0.963 from $0.974/$0.977 at Monday's close, UES was $0.0764/$0.0768 after $0.0781/$0.079, LUKoil edged down to $8.99/$9.16 from $9.35/$9.49 and Norilsk Nickel was $6.95/$7.10 after $7.15/$7.30.
